clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text, with no own-terms end and no later instrument found by the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog; 48 CFR 22.901 (eCFR through 2026-10-19) restates the policy under the order; checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The clause declares the anti-age-discrimination policy for Federal contractors and subcontractors and directs agencies to give notice of it in procurement regulations. 48 CFR 22.901 as held (eCFR through 2026-10-19) states the policy under Executive Order 11141 and other current CFR texts cite it; the bounded searches found no amendment, revocation or supersession.

research_rationale:
EO 11141 (29 FR 2477, signed 1964-02-12) declares it the policy of the Executive Branch that contractors and subcontractors on Federal contracts shall not discriminate in employment because of age except on the basis of a bona fide occupational qualification, retirement plan or statutory requirement, and shall not specify a maximum age limit in solicitations or advertisements for employees on Government contracts except on the same basis; it directs the head of each department and agency to take appropriate action to enunciate the policy and directs that the Federal Procurement Regulations and the Armed Services Procurement Regulation be amended to give continuous notice of it. The held Federal Register original has no sunset, condition or revocation clause. The held eCFR text of 48 CFR 22.901 (FAR, amended through 2026-10-19) restates the policy as the Government policy under Executive Order 11141, and the held eCFR texts of 32 CFR 191.1 and 191.5, 18 CFR 1316.6 and 23 CFR 260.115 and the 5 U.S.C. 3301 note (Ex. Ord. No. 11141) cite or print it. the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and show no amendment, revocation or supersession.
